title: Sausage and Mash with Caramelised Onion Gravy
subtitle: The British pub classic done properly
excerpt: Good pork sausages baked until caramelised, served on generous mashed potato with a rich onion gravy made from slowly cooked onions and beef stock. The test of a pub kitchen, done at home.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sausage and mash is one of the quintessential British dishes and is sometimes called bangers and mash, bangers being slang for sausages that dates to World War I when sausages were made with so much water that they burst loudly in the pan. The caramelised onion gravy became the standard accompaniment in British pub cooking during the 1990s restaurant revival of traditional British food.

content.text: The onion gravy is what makes this dish. The onions need a long, slow cook until they are deep brown and sweet, at least 25 minutes over low heat. Rush this and the gravy will be pale and sharp rather than dark and sweet. Bake the sausages in the oven rather than frying them so they colour evenly all over without splitting. The mash should be very buttery.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Put the sausages in a roasting tin with a drizzle of oil. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until deep golden all over.

Make the onion gravy: heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook very slowly for 25 minutes, stirring often, until they are deep golden and sweet. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Add the wine, let it bubble, then add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, and thyme. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. Remove the thyme.
While the onions cook, boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender. Drain well and mash with the butter and hot milk. Season generously.
Plate the mash, lay the sausages on top, and pour the onion gravy over everything.
